quest.title: Calling from the Masters of the Night-Wind
quest.description: After happening across a baby Iktomisaurus, a mysterious presence guides you into the Masters of the Night-Wind's settlement...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x275, Mora x26025, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.num: Memories Flowing With Color: Act I
chapter.title: Calling from the Masters of the Night-Wind

talks.objective: Go to the Masters of the Night-Wind's tribal settlement

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, we really did get teleported...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But where's the way out?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... It seems like this place is completely sealed off. Doesn't look like there's an exit anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's take a look around and see what we can find.

talks.objective: Go to the settlement of the Masters of the Night-Wind

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *gasp* Something's hiding behind that statue!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, it's a baby Iktomisaurus. So cute... although, why is it staring at us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What is this place...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Who are you...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... How long was Paimon out?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon locked eyes with that baby Iktomisaurus for like, a second, and then she was suddenly pulled into this strange place with a huuuge Iktomisaur!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, same here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Any idea what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}? Hey, what's wrong?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Look! It's that baby Iktomisaur — seems like it wants us to follow it. Paimon's adventurous side says we have to see where this leads!

talks.objective: Go to the settlement of the Masters of the Night-Wind

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wonder if we're allowed in here... Oh. The door opened all by itself. Taking that as a yes!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw! The Iktomisaur from earlier, it's really here!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's the one who summoned us...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then let's go introduce ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello there, um...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, probably doesn't understand what we're saying... Doesn't look like any cogs are turning in there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoops, sorry! No offense intended!
You there — you dare disrespect our elder!?
Oh, you mean... I see, I see. Sorry, my mistake. Apparently, you are here by invitation, in which case it's my job to make you feel welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Some introductions are in order. I am Caholom, one of the priests of our tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: And this is our Iktomisaur Elder, the Great Tlapopoctiztetl. A living totem among the Masters of the Night-Wind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that's quite a tongue-twister...

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: In truth, we usually go with "Elder Tlapo" for short. You're welcome to do the same.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We were invited here in a very... unusual way.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Ah, I assume you're referring to our elder's special ability.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Elder Tlapo has been alive for many centuries, and harbors secrets that even we priests are at a loss to explain, so your reaction is entirely natural.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: But one thing I can say for sure is that Elder Tlapo has appointed the two of you to an extremely important task. For this reason, I would like to ask you to undergo a test.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What sort of task? And what kind of test?

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: If it's alright with you, I'll take you to see our chief. He's in a much better position to answer your questions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... okay, sure.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Very well. Then please follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: You can use this scroll to go directly to the Obsidian Altar, where the chief is.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Don't worry, it's just one of the many mystical abilities of our tribe.

talks.objective: Meet with the Chief of the Masters of the Night-Wind

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, what was that just now?

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: One of the routine duties of a priest. We attempt to contact the spirits of our ancestors to seek epiphanies and revelations.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: The chief is just over there. Please wait here while I have a word with him — I'll just be a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, the Masters of the Night-Wind are definitely living up to their reputation as the mysterious ones.

dialogues.speaker: Caholom
dialogues.text: Alright, I've told the chief why we're here, and now you may speak with him. Right this way.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: So, you two are the appointed ones? I am Chief Biram. Welcome, and thank you for your patience.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...So tall...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Unusually so. Yes, I am aware. But I assure you, it's no cause for alarm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh — no, of course not! Sorry, Paimon just reacted without thinking...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's this about us being "appointed"?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Ah yes, Caholom told me about that. As outsiders to our tribe, this is probably the first you've heard of such appointments. I'm sure the whole thing seems very confusing.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Throughout our history, only members of the Masters of the Night-Wind have been appointed to undertake these tasks. This is the first time an outsider has ever been chosen.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Allow me to explain. Our tribe has an old tradition of recording history in the form of woven scrolls.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: And not just our own history. We record the legends and heroic feats of all other tribes as well.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: It is a tradition we have observed for many centuries. We treat it as a solemn duty.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: However, when a major event occurs that affects all of Natlan, we record it on a different kind of scroll used for this exact purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: And these scrolls can only be woven by someone of the Iktomisaur Elder's choosing.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: When the Iktomisaur Elder senses a major change in the Ley Lines, it will issue a formal declaration to appoint a creator for this scroll.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, so you mean...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Elder Tlapo sensed a Ley Line change quite some time ago, but had not yet designated the scroll-weavers... until you arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, but... Just so you're aware, we don't know the first thing about weaving scrolls.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: As a matter of fact, that does not surprise me at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How come?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: In the two hundred years that Elder Tlapo has held this position, none of the appointed ones have ever been experienced scroll-weavers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does that mean two hundred years of major historical events have gone unrecorded?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: No, they all submitted scrolls in time. Yet each of them claimed it was not their own work, but a "gift from the spirits."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Man... this tribe gets more mysterious by the second.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Yes, well... that is the part that troubles me.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: The notion that we have to rely on esoteric things like "gifts from the spirits" to record historical events of such great importance... it is unsettling.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... That's pretty surprising to hear, coming from the chief of this tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I can imagine. You probably see the Masters of the Night-Wind as a people shrouded in mystery, who pride ourselves on our arcane practices.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: But I am something of an exception. I may be the chief, but when it comes to our traditions, I am in fact a proponent of change and reform.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I have dedicated my energies to deciphering the many mysteries of our tribe. In doing so, I hope to establish clearer rules that will help sustain our traditions in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that sounds great! So have you figured out the mystery of the "gift from the spirits"?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Sadly not... It is something I have been investigating for a long time, but I have yet to uncover what this "gift" truly refers to.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Only a small handful of events over the years have been recorded on these special scrolls, with decades between each one.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: And by the time the next scroll-weaver is appointed, my time as chief will be long gone. I will not be in a position to investigate as thoroughly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: While I haven't yet gotten to the bottom of the matter, I have made some progress. But the only way I can develop my theories further is with the cooperation of the appointed ones.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And that's why you want to put us through this test.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Precisely. It's nothing to be worried about — simply a means of validating my current hypothesis. It shouldn't take you long, nor will it put you in any danger.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright. So what does it involve, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I can explain everything in detail when we get to the site of the test. But first, please wait a moment while I change out of the Soul-Shielding Cloak.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: This garb is one of our important cultural relics, handed down by generations of chiefs. It is only to be worn when conducting certain ceremonies.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Biram removes his cloak and carefully hands it to a priest for safekeeping.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Please follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Do you see this scroll? If you touch it, you will enter a hidden space.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Today's test is, quite simply, to find a way to escape that space.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's it?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I assure you, it's not as easy as it sounds. If you cannot find your own way out, I will of course intervene to bring you back here.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: But then, we will be no closer to solving this mystery...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Good. Simply touch the scroll to begin the test.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are so many woven scrolls here. Paimon remembers seeing some of them before in other tribes. They seem to record historical events.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This one really stands out from the rest. For starters, it's the biggest of them all. Wonder what story it tells?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The colors are very distinctive, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, you're right...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Over there, something just flashed! {NICKNAME}, did you catch that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe that's how we get out...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...By seeing things we couldn't see before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, right! Paimon's with you!

dialogues.speaker: Strange Machine
dialogues.text: (There's some sort of a machine here. Probably used for weaving.)

dialogues.speaker: Giant Woven Scroll
dialogues.text: (This scroll has purposely been hung in the very middle of the ceiling. Whatever it means, it must be significant.)

dialogues.speaker: Stack of Woven Scrolls
dialogues.text: (A large pile of woven scrolls. The thick layer of dust indicates that they've been here a long time.)

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: You may begin whenever you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, we finally got out!

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: It is just as I thought. You are indeed capable of undertaking this mission.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did this prove your theory?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Yes. You saw many distinctive-looking scrolls there, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure did...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: This specific kind of scroll was left to us by our ancestors. Upon investigation, I discovered what sets it apart is the use of a color not featured in ordinary scrolls.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: It is a most mysterious color that most people cannot even detect. I myself had to employ special techniques to confirm its existence.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Yet there are those who are born with a natural ability to perceive it. And that is why I wanted to test you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: That space you just entered was an exhibition room for storing this variety of woven scrolls.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Centuries ago, a great shaman by the name of Huitzilin put in place a security measure, so that anyone who entered the room without permission would become trapped inside.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: It exists to this day, and although I have not managed to decipher how it works, I have at least found out how to turn it on and off.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Once someone is trapped inside, it is all but impossible for them to escape without outside help — unless they share the great shaman's ability to perceive that strange color.

choices.text: I think I know what you mean.

response.speaker: Biram
response.text: Clearly, you must have this ability... Which leads me to believe that our Iktomisaur Elder can sense this ability in people, and that it appoints a scroll-weaver on this basis.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Another secret power? {NICKNAME}, you are full of mysteries...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, having this ability doesn't change the fact that neither of us know where to start with weaving a scroll.

response.speaker: Biram
response.text: Don't worry about that. The method for weaving this kind of scroll appears to be largely the same as for an ordinary scroll. The main difference is in the dye that gives it its unique color.

response.speaker: Biram
response.text: If my suspicions are correct, this dye is the key to weaving the scroll — and your special ability is the key to obtaining it.

response.speaker: Biram
response.text: The dyeing process is also a little different from the norm, but I don't anticipate any major issues there. As long as you two can source the dye itself, I can assist with the application.

response.speaker: Biram
response.text: Great. Then please use your abilities to source the necessary ingredients, and in the meantime I will have someone prepare some fabric for test-dyeing.

response.speaker: Biram
response.text: We'll make a few sample pieces to test out my hypothesis, and if that goes well, we can begin the scroll in earnest.

response.speaker: Biram
response.text: If you agree to help, you can expect to be handsomely rewarded once this is all over. So, what are your thoughts?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think with the ability to help comes the responsibility to do so.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Agreed! Especially if there's a reward in it! ...What is the reward, by the way? Is it food? Paimon hopes it's food.

response.speaker: Biram
response.text: Given the stakes involved for our tribe, I was thinking a substantial sum of Mora would be appropriate.... Surely that would be preferable to just a free meal?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mora works too! Anyway, how do we go about finding these ingredients? Or are we supposed to just keep walking around Natlan until we stumble across them...?

response.speaker: Biram
response.text: Thankfully not. I have already identified a location where I suspect they may be found, and I've arranged for someone to guide you there.

response.speaker: Biram
response.text: Your guide is waiting just outside. You can set off at your leisure.

choices.text: I did see a certain color in there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, check it out, the graffiti on the wall is glowing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Masters of the Night-Wind... and by the looks of it, masters of nightlife too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aha, there IS something hiding here! Yup, this looks like our ticket outta this place!
